Name: SupporterMod
Description: v0.6.3 - Adds /sup and /supporters as aliases. Found by testing as a non-OP player rather than as an admin: the first thing instinctively typed was /sup, which returned Command not found. Also documents the discoverability finding - commands RUN for every player regardless of permissions, but the command tree the client uses for tab completion is filtered by CommandTreeBuilder through hasPermission, so a command whose node has not been granted simply does not appear while typing. Players can therefore use everything and still never find it. The node follows the plugin manifest: thepeoplesserver.supportermod.supporter, with each subcommand appended. FactionMod has the same shape (thepeoplesserver.factionmod.f) and the same gap on this server. ---  v0.6.2 - FIX: the LuckPerms sync never ran. The live log shows SupporterMod reporting LuckPerms NOT found at 10:22:54 and the server enabling LuckPerms at 10:23:05 - eleven seconds later. setup() runs long before other plugins are enabled, so probing for LuckPerms there caches a wrong answer for the entire session. LuckPerms is now resolved lazily on first use (a grant or a login), by which point everything is up, and PermissionSync is always installed when nodes are configured rather than being chosen at startup. Also declares LuckPerms:LuckPerms in OptionalDependencies, which both fixes load ordering and lets this plugins classloader see LuckPerms classes at all - the same class of problem as the JDBC driver in 0.2.1. If LuckPerms really is missing, the first attempt logs a loud one-time warning naming the cause instead of silently skipping, because silently skipping means a paying customer without the perk they bought. ---  v0.6.1 - Homes are now automatic. /supporter grant only ever wrote to SupporterMods own database, so every perk gated on isSupporter switched on by itself while homes - owned by EliteEssentials and resolved through LuckPerms - did not. SupporterMod now pushes the configured nodes (luckPermsNodes, default eliteessentials.command.home.limit.10) into LuckPerms as TEMPORARY nodes expiring at the end of the grace window. Temporary is the point: a permanent node plus a removal job means two systems that must agree about when somebody stopped paying, and they eventually will not - a missed reconcile, a server down over the expiry, a crash between two writes. A node carrying its own expiry cannot drift, because LuckPerms removes it whether or not this plugin is running. Renewals use REPLACE_EXISTING_IF_DURATION_LONGER so buying more time extends the node and can never shorten it. Sync fires on grant, revoke, chargeback, the nightly reconcile, and every login - the login case both delivers gift purchases that had no UUID when bought and self-heals a node lost to a LuckPerms outage or a restore from backup. All of it is best-effort and asynchronous: a permissions write failing must never fail the purchase that triggered it, because the money has already moved, so failures are logged loudly instead. LuckPerms is an OPTIONAL dependency - absent, this degrades to a no-op and every other perk still works. 66 tests. ---  v0.6.0 - PHASE 3: homes. Delivered as configuration, not code, because EliteEssentials already owns /home, /sethome and /delhome on this server and resolves the limit through LuckPerms nodes (eliteessentials.command.home.limit.<N>, homes.limit.<N>, or unlimited). Building a second home system inside SupporterMod would mean two competing /home commands reimplementing a plugin already running. The defaultHomeSlots and supporterHomeSlots keys are therefore DESCRIPTIVE: they drive what /supporter perks tells players, and must be kept in step with the real EliteEssentials and LuckPerms values or the plugin advertises a perk that does not match reality. Verified before recommending the change: lowering the limit only makes /sethome return LIMIT_REACHED - HomeService has no bulk delete, so homes already set above the new cap are kept and stay usable, and nobody loses a home they were using. Adds /supporter perks, listing what supporters get and what the player currently has, as a single source of truth for the store page. ---  v0.5.0 - PHASE 5: tokens and the supporter shop. Supporters earn tokens for tenure and spend them on trails: /supporter tokens, /supporter shop, /supporter buy. Two free trails so every supporter has the perk immediately, four behind a token ladder. THE BALANCE IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED - earned is totalMonths x tokensPerMonth, spent is the sum of recorded purchases, balance is the difference. A stored counter can be double-credited by a retried grant, drift after a crash between the write and the credit, or silently disagree with the purchase history; a derived one cannot. Same argument as total_months itself. Purchases are idempotent at the database level: supporter_unlocks has a composite primary key on (uuid, item_id) and the insert does nothing on conflict, so a double-click cannot charge twice - refused by the schema rather than by a check that could race. Closes PLAN open decision 3, chargeback vs expiry. They are different events: an expiry or revoke ends entitlement but KEEPS tenure, because the player did pay for that time and keeps the tokens it earned; a chargeback means the money came back, so /supporter chargeback removes the tenure that was never paid for and the tokens follow automatically, with no separate ledger to keep in step. Items already bought are never removed and the balance clamps at zero. Nothing here touches the bucks economy - tokens have no exchange path in either direction. Schema migration V4. 59 tests. ---  v0.4.1 - FIX: trail particles never disappeared. Of the 598 particle systems the server ships, 540 have NO LifeSpan - they are designed to be attached to something persistent such as a projectile or a torch, and spawned free-standing at a world position they simply stay there forever. The first trail list picked six of those by plausible name, and the live world ended up carpeted in glowing blobs. Defaults are now drawn only from the 49 effects with a finite LifeSpan, favouring low spawner counts because a trail emits continuously. Before adding a trail, confirm the effect expires by grepping its .particlesystem file for LifeSpan - no LifeSpan line means do not use it. tools/ScanParticles.java lists the safe set. Particles already in the world clear when the client reloads the area. ---  v0.4.0 - PHASE 4: particle trails. Supporters pick a trail with /supporter trail <name>; any player can hide everyone elses with /supporter trails off. Trails are stock Hytale particle effects chosen by config id, so no custom art is bundled and an admin can repoint or cheapen one without a rebuild. This is the most performance-sensitive thing in the plugin - it runs continuously, for every supporter at once - so four controls bound it: it emits ONLY when a player has actually moved trailMinMoveDistance since their last emit (most online players are stationary most of the time, so this is the biggest saving); the particle goes to a VIEWER LIST of players within trailViewDistance rather than being broadcast, and never to anyone who has hidden trails; maxConcurrentTrails caps the work per tick so cost does not scale with sales; and the scheduler thread only resolves the world before handing off with world.execute, so every component read and particle spawn happens on the world thread. Schema migration V3. New config keys are backfilled per key, not with a whole-map guard, so a live supporter.json that predates a trail still receives it. 47 tests. ---  v0.3.1 - FIX: the chat tag did not appear on the live server. lucko:mini-chat-formatter is also installed, also sets a PlayerChatEvent formatter, and at NORMAL priority ran after us and replaced ours. Its configured format is <meta:jobtitle> <prefix><username><suffix>: <message>, which is where the rank shown in chat comes from via LuckPerms. Winning that race by registering later would have meant discarding the rank, prefix and suffix - reimplementing another plugins job to add six characters. SupporterMod now registers at EventPriority.LAST and WRAPS whichever formatter is already in place instead of replacing it, so the line becomes the supporter tag followed by the chat plugins own output, whatever it is configured to be. If mini-chat-formatter is ever removed the delegate is simply the servers DEFAULT_FORMATTER and this still works. The chosen colour now applies to the tag rather than the username, because the username belongs to the delegate - which also means the colour shows for a supporter who has not set a title. Note mini-chat-formatter logs one cosmetic warning per boot that another plugin set the formatter; it does not re-apply, so the wrapper survives. ---  v0.3.0 - PHASE 2: chat identity. Supporters get a [Supporter] tag, an optional custom title and a chat colour, set with /supporter title and /supporter colour. The chat handler NEVER cancels PlayerChatEvent and never broadcasts anything itself - it calls setFormatter, so the server keeps ownership of delivery. That is what makes it safe alongside FactionMod: FactionMod cancels the event when a player has faction chat toggled on and re-broadcasts to their faction only, so a plugin that also cancelled and broadcast server-wide would leak private faction messages to everybody. With a formatter, if FactionMod has already cancelled then ours is simply never invoked. Titles are validated for length, control characters and a configurable blocklist - the rejection message deliberately does not name the matched word, because that would turn the blocklist into an oracle somebody can probe. Colours must be on the allowedChatColors list and are normalised to the configured spelling. Identity lives in its own table and OUTLIVES a lapse: an expired title stops rendering but is not deleted, so renewing restores exactly what the player had. Schema migration V2. 40 tests. ---  v0.2.2 - FIX: plugin data now lives in plugins/SupporterMod/ rather than the path getDataDirectory() returns, which is under mods/. The asset module scans mods/ for asset packs, so the database folder was picked up as a malformed pack and logged "Skipping pack at ThePeoplesServer_SupporterMod: missing or invalid manifest.json" on every boot. FactionMod uses plugins/<Name>/ for exactly this reason. If you are upgrading from 0.2.1, move mods/ThePeoplesServer_SupporterMod/supporter.db to plugins/SupporterMod/ to keep existing grants. --- v0.2.1 - FIX: the first live deploy failed with 'No suitable driver found for jdbc:sqlite:...' even though sqlite-jdbc was correctly shaded and META-INF/services/java.sql.Driver was present in the jar. DriverManager performs its ServiceLoader discovery once against the system classloader, and Hytale loads each plugin in its own PluginClassLoader, which the system classloader cannot see - so the driver never registers and DriverManager has nothing to return. Now connects through SQLiteDataSource, which holds the driver directly and never consults that global registry. This also keeps SupporterMod out of the way of the other plugins here that shade their own sqlite-jdbc (Windskull's Survival, Hunger and Thirst all do) rather than adding a fourth driver to a registry shared between them. Note for the record: SQLite works fine on this server - the earlier recon claim that there was no SQLite precedent was wrong. --- v0.2.0 - Phase 1 complete. The entitlement core is now wired to the server: SupporterPlugin lifecycle, the /supporter command tree, player-join claiming and the nightly reconcile job. Admin subcommands (grant, revoke, reconcile) extend CommandBase rather than AbstractPlayerCommand, because AbstractPlayerCommand requires a player and Tebex delivers purchases from the console - a player-only grant command would fail on every real purchase while working perfectly in testing. No optional positional arguments anywhere: withOptionalArg registers a named flag rendered as [--name=?], so a bare positional word is rejected as an unexpected required parameter. Startup failure is surfaced rather than swallowed - the server bundles no JDBC driver, so sqlite-jdbc unpacks a native library at first use and can fail at runtime in a way no compile check catches; if that happens every command reports the reason instead of the server booting with a silently dead supporter system that accepts grants and loses them. --- v0.1.0 - Supporter rank for The People's Server. Entitlement core only: grant, renewal, grace period and nightly expiry reconcile, backed by SQLite. Renewals extend from the existing expiry rather than from now, so buying early never costs time. Grants carrying a payment-provider transaction id are applied at most once, because Tebex retries delivery until the server acknowledges it. Nothing in this plugin touches combat, claims, power, outpost income, KOTJ scoring or the bucks economy.
